description: VVC's Adaptive Loop Filter (ALF) decomposed. ALF is a content-adapted Wiener filter that replaces HEVC's SAO. Each CTU's samples are classified into one of 25 categories based on local activity and direction; each category gets its own diamond-shaped FIR filter with coefficients signalled by the encoder. The filter is in-loop, applied AFTER deblocking. Cross-component ALF (CC-ALF) additionally uses luma to enhance chroma.

sub_mechanisms.name: diamond_filter_shape
sub_mechanisms.definition: Three supported shapes — 5x5, 7x7, 9x9 diamonds (so 9, 13, 21 taps respectively, centered on the target sample). The shape is selected per CTU.
sub_mechanisms.why: Diamond shape (vs square) gives directional reach with fewer taps — 21 taps for a 9-tap radius vs 81 for a 9x9 square. The radii cover the typical correlation length of compression noise without paying for irrelevant corner taps.

sub_mechanisms.name: block_classification
sub_mechanisms.definition: Each 4x4 block is classified into one of 25 categories based on 5 directional activity bins (horizontal, vertical, two diagonals, isotropic) crossed with 5 activity-strength bins (computed from gradient sums).
sub_mechanisms.why: Different categories of local structure benefit from different filters. Flat regions want low-pass; edges want directional preservation; texture wants minimal filtering. 25 classes is the empirical sweet spot — finer doesn't help, coarser loses adaptivity.

sub_mechanisms.name: gradient_based_direction
sub_mechanisms.definition: Direction classification computes horizontal, vertical, and two diagonal gradient sums over each 4x4 block; the largest determines the direction class.
sub_mechanisms.why: Gradient-based direction is fast and robust. Captures the dominant local structure without needing edge detection. Same computation could be reused for other tools but is currently ALF-specific in VVC.

sub_mechanisms.name: activity_based_strength
sub_mechanisms.definition: Activity strength uses the sum of all gradient magnitudes; quantised into 5 bins (low → high activity).
sub_mechanisms.why: High-activity regions (textured) tolerate less filtering than low-activity (flat). Strength-classification lets each direction's filter be applied with different aggressiveness.

sub_mechanisms.name: coefficient_signalling_APS
sub_mechanisms.definition: Filter coefficients are signalled in Adaptation Parameter Sets (APS). Each APS can carry multiple filter sets; a CTU can reference an APS by ID + select one filter set within it.
sub_mechanisms.why: APS-based signalling lets the encoder pre-define multiple filter sets at the slice header (cheap), then per-CTU select which one to use (very cheap). Decouples coefficient signalling cost from per-CTU filter selection cost.

sub_mechanisms.name: filter_coefficient_inheritance
sub_mechanisms.definition: Each CTU's filter selection can inherit coefficients from the APS or from prior CTUs' filters; only the SELECTION needs signalling, not the coefficients each time.
sub_mechanisms.why: Coefficients are expensive to signal (16-21 of them per filter). Inheriting from a smaller set + selecting by index drops the per-CTU cost from ~100 bits to ~4 bits. The compression cost difference is significant across millions of CTUs.

sub_mechanisms.name: cross_component_alf
sub_mechanisms.definition: CC-ALF: an additional ALF stage where chroma samples are filtered using LUMA neighbourhood samples as input. A small 8-tap filter is applied.
sub_mechanisms.why: Chroma edges tend to align with luma edges (cross-component correlation in YCbCr). Using luma as input lets the chroma filter recover edge sharpness that intra-channel filtering can't. Cheap addition that gives ~0.5% bitrate saving on chroma.

sub_mechanisms.name: alf_enable_disable_per_CTU
sub_mechanisms.definition: A 1-bit flag per CTU enables or disables ALF for that CTU. Encoder picks via R-D cost (some CTUs are better off without ALF).
sub_mechanisms.why: Some content actively suffers from ALF (sharp screen content, very low QP clean encodes). Per-CTU disable lets the encoder skip the filter where it'd cause harm, at minimal signalling cost.

sub_mechanisms.name: luma_chroma_separate_filters
sub_mechanisms.definition: Luma and chroma have entirely separate ALF systems (different coefficient sets, different shapes, different classification).
sub_mechanisms.why: Luma and chroma have very different statistics (luma is high-detail, chroma is low-frequency in 4:2:0). One-size-fits-all filters would be sub-optimal for both. Separate systems let each be tuned to its channel.

sub_mechanisms.name: fixed_filter_fallback
sub_mechanisms.definition: If no APS-signalled filter is suitable, ALF can fall back to one of 16 pre-defined fixed filters (built into the standard).
sub_mechanisms.why: Sometimes the encoder can't justify the signalling cost of a custom filter set but still wants ALF. Fixed filters give a baseline at zero per-CTU coefficient cost — a free option that captures ~half the gain of a fully-custom filter.

derivation_rules.name: content_classification_enables_per_block_adaptation
if: each block is classified by local activity + direction
then: the filter applied is the best one for that block's category
derivation_rules.why: ALF's gain over a uniform filter is exactly the gain from adaptation. 25 classes is enough to capture the major content variations within typical frames; finer classification helps marginally at higher signalling cost.

derivation_rules.name: wiener_filter_minimises_squared_error
if: filter coefficients are derived by solving Wiener-Hopf equations
then: the filter is optimal (in MSE sense) for the given input statistics
derivation_rules.why: Wiener filtering is the closed-form optimal linear filter for noise removal under MSE. ALF coefficients are essentially Wiener filters fit to the local autocorrelation. Optimal in theory, near-optimal in practice given finite signalling precision.

derivation_rules.name: aps_signalling_decouples_definition_from_selection
if: filter sets are pre-defined in APS
then: per-CTU bit cost is selection-only, not coefficient-redefinition
derivation_rules.why: APS pays the cost ONCE per slice; per-CTU just references an APS by ID + filter index. Splits a 100-bit-per-CTU cost into a ~100-bit-per-slice + ~4-bit-per-CTU cost, dramatically reducing total signalling.

derivation_rules.name: cross_component_filtering_exploits_yuv_correlation
if: chroma is filtered using luma neighbourhood input
then: chroma edges align with luma edges, gaining sharpness
derivation_rules.why: YCbCr's luma and chroma channels are correlated at edge boundaries. A linear model on luma input can predict chroma edge structure that pure intra-chroma filtering misses. Same insight as CCLM in intra prediction, applied to in-loop filtering.
